content.thinking:
Best so far is lr=0.000436 with wd=0.2 giving 3.5638, with wd trending better as it increases from 0.1 to 0.2. With 96 credits left, I want to test whether this trend continues, so I'll try pushing wd higher to 0.3 and 0.4 at the same learning rate.

I need to budget carefully: reserve enough credits for a final confirmation run at 16B tokens (costing 64 credits for one seed), so I should spend maybe 32-40 credits on further exploration at 2B tokens (cost 8 per run) for another 4-5 runs. The target tolerance is generous—0.0008 loss tolerance is close to the noise floor of about 0.0013—so I don't need extreme precision, just to land in the right neighborhood of the optimum before confirming.

I'll test wd=0.3 and wd=0.5 at lr=0.000436, plus check wd=0.2 with lr around 0.0004-0.0005 to see if the optimal lr shifts with wd. With 96 credits total, four exploratory runs would cost 32, leaving 64 for a single full confirmation run—tight but workable, or I could trim to three runs to leave a small buffer.

Also adding wd=0.2 lr=0.0004 and wd=0.2 lr=0.0005 to the exploration batch.

input.command:
for cfg in "0.000436 0.3" "0.000436 0.5" "0.0004 0.2" "0.0005 0.2"; do
  set -- $cfg
  lr=$1; wd=$2
  echo "=== lr=$lr wd=$wd ==="
  lab run batch=2048 tokens=2 lr=$lr wd=$wd seeds=1 2>&1
done
echo "---"
lab status
